risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: lagged GMM only, no external instrument, causal wording ('impact'), bidirectional Granger causality found.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: too_harsh: a PCA index of mobile, fixed and internet use does capture ICT diffusion; the unit problem ('1% increase' of a mean-zero index) is an interpretation flaw, so moderate fits.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: wide panel, but Table 4 obs (3496, 1235/988/779/494) imply more countries than the stated 171 (57/48/41/25).
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: RGDP level in US$ treated as growth, with Table 4 max 100 and min 0.0003 inconsistent with billions of dollars.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree (serious): lag order unreported, authors misread the Table 11 row/column layout, stars inconsistent with p-values.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: one model per sample, no robustness, text signs conflict with table.
risk_of_bias.why: Serious stands: causal framing, only internal lags for endogeneity, and the authors' headline numbers (0.007, -34) come from the wrong cells.

problems: Core error: record follows the authors' transposed reading of Table 11, contradicted by Table 10 p-values (entire-sample ICT row RGDP col 0.0080 vs Table 10 RGDP not-> ICT p=0.7980 shows the authors' table is itself inconsistent there). Record's 'internal inconsistency' in signs disappears under the table layout. Record says outcome 'Real GDP' growth effect 0.007%, which is not supported. Stars in Table 11 are inconsistent with p (e.g. 0.0010**).
